answer.evidence: Two mirrored chairs. In the column scan at x=8 and x=23, rows 10-12 are a light gold top band and the silhouette widens from 20 to 28 over rows 10-13, which suggests a receding top plane. Row 13 is a darker stripe, row 14 is lighter again, and row 15 is a dark edge line. Below that, rows 16-24 are a vertical front face made of a grey-beige and cream cushion with a brown lower border, about 10 rows. The side strips at x=5-7 and x=15-17 are armrests or backrest, which are exempt. The center pedestal table is a small decor-like fixture and is not the main body. The seat top is only moderately clear because the stripe pattern in rows 13-15 is ambiguous, but it reads as a top plane with a front-edge line followed by a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is two small chairs with cream/tan woven backs and brown frames. The board is small, so I judged mostly from the measured facts. It has 14 visible tones per tile, above the hedge (9) and close to the cheese stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a brown tint rather than being a black sticker line. The seat backs show a light-to-dark ramp of about 5 steps with slat and grain variation, similar to the bench and stall wood. The pieces are simple and a little small, but they would sit next to the references without looking thinner or flatter.
